ui.title: Patch 26.21 tier list by role
ui.subtitle: A static table with the recommended picks, patch changes and watchlist champions for every role.
ui.provisional: Provisional rankings: the patch has just launched and role-specific data is still limited.
ui.noResultsHint: Try removing a filter or searching for another name.
ui.noTierPicks: No confirmed picks in this tier for this role.
ui.emptyTierNote: Without role-specific data we will not promote picks to S+ or S.
ui.tapHint: Tap a card to read the full breakdown.
ui.noStats: There is no verified data for this champion in the initial patch sample. We do not display invented numbers.
ui.compareEmpty: Select two or three champions with the + button on each card.
ui.compareLimit: You can compare up to 3 champions.
ui.compareHint: Verified data is kept separate from the editorial assessment.
ui.finderIntro: Answer four questions and we will suggest three champions. The suggestions use transparent editorial rules based on tier, difficulty, playstyle and rank; they are not a rank-specific statistical model.
ui.finderRuleNote: Transparent rules: we prioritise tier, difficulty, playstyle and rank fit. We do not use rank-specific win rates because we do not have a reliable sample.
ui.finderReasonDifficulty: Its {difficulty} difficulty matches what you asked for.
ui.finderReasonFallback: It is a well-rounded option in this role.
ui.finderNoResults: There are not enough champions for that combination. Try another setup.
ui.randomIntro: Choose a role and let the roulette decide. The result comes from the champions reviewed in this tier list.
ui.randomHint: The real League Roulette also lets you filter by role and verify your matches.
ui.statSample: 206,610 Ranked Solo/Duo games analysed by ggez.gg

tierDescriptions.S+: Reserved for picks with strong, consistent role-specific evidence.
tierDescriptions.S: No confirmed candidates: the initial data cannot isolate a clear role dominator.
tierDescriptions.A: Our main recommendations for this patch, always provisional.
tierDescriptions.B: Viable picks with conditions, recent nerfs or samples that still need confirmation.
tierDescriptions.C: Options that have lost power or depend heavily on context and matchups.

championPoolNote: Portraits come from Data Dragon (16.21.1). The champion list is an editorial selection based on the official patch notes and the first patch data, not the full roster.

sources.label: Official League of Legends Patch 26.21 notes — Riot Games
Champion statistics and tier list — Mobalytics

champions.name: Sion
champions.why: He gains more health per level and a harder-hitting fully charged ultimate. He remains a tank with engage and the ability to create space in fights.
champions.changes: Health growth: 87 → 95. R (Unstoppable Onslaught): damage increases by up to 200% during the first 3 seconds of channeling. The tooltip also now shows the correct bonus AD ratios.
strengths: Holds up in long side lanes and extended fights.
His ultimate punishes poor positioning and starts fights.
He does not need to win lane to provide value.
weaknesses: Struggles against percentage damage and highly mobile teams.
His R is easy to dodge when used without setup.
champions.profile: Players who prefer durable tanks, starting fights and playing around objectives.

stats.note: ggez.gg data for all ranks; not Top-specific.

champions.name: Darius
champions.why: His Q cooldown drops to 4 seconds at max rank, which improves extended trades. His lane pressure remains high if you punish mistakes.
champions.changes: Q (Decimate): cooldown 9/8/7/6/5s → 9/8/7/6/4s.
strengths: Turns lane mistakes into large advantages.
A major threat in extended fights.
weaknesses: Can be kited by range and crowd control.
Depends on hitting the Q blade.
champions.profile: Aggressive players who understand trades and want to pressure lane.

stats.note: ggez.gg data for all ranks; the change is small and does not invalidate the Q buff.

champions.name: Volibear
champions.why: A solid option for dueling, durability and pressure. He received no direct changes, so his value depends more on performance and team fit.
champions.changes: No direct changes in 26.21. He remains an editorial pick for players who want a lane bruiser.
strengths: Good early duels and tower pressure.
weaknesses: Can fall behind on resources if set back.
Struggles against kiting compositions.
champions.profile: Players who want a durable bruiser with a straightforward side-lane and objective plan.

champions.name: Garen
champions.why: An accessible pick for players who want consistency and a clear game plan. His inclusion is editorial and does not imply a buff this patch.
champions.changes: No direct changes in 26.21.
weaknesses: Little ranged pressure.
Can be kited by mobile compositions.
champions.profile: New players or anyone who wants a direct champion to focus on fundamentals.

champions.name: Yone
champions.why: He remains a strong duelist, but his Q loses AD ratio. We place him in B: the nerf is moderate and his mechanical ceiling is still high.
champions.changes: Q (Mortal Steel): AD ratio 110% → 105%. No other kit changes.
strengths: High mechanical ceiling and side-lane pressure.
Can start or finish fights with R.
weaknesses: Punishes his own mistakes heavily.
The nerf slightly lowers his sustained damage.
champions.profile: Experienced duelists willing to invest time in mechanics.

champions.name: Varus
champions.why: The Q and W adjustments are aimed at limiting his Top variant. We keep him in provisional C here: the change hits his W-max pattern, even though the overall data is not Top-specific.
champions.changes: Q: max damage now scales better with channel time. W: less on-hit and per-stack damage, but better AD/AP ratios and more reward for charging Q.
weaknesses: His Top variant loses power with the adjustment.
Fragile against dives and mobile champions.
champions.profile: Poke players willing to adapt their build; not a Top pick for everyone.

stats.note: All-rank data: it may mostly reflect his bot-lane variant, not Top.

champions.name: Taliyah
champions.why: She gains E damage and keeps the 225% monster damage. She can clear camps more safely and punish grouped enemies with crowd control.
strengths: More comfortable jungle clear after the buff.
Strong rotations and ganks with her wall.
weaknesses: Needs good positioning to land combos.
Can struggle against aggressive invading junglers.
champions.profile: Players who enjoy mage junglers, zone control and rotations.

champions.name: Shyvana
champions.why: With no direct changes, she keeps a clear profile: fast clearing, scaling and sustained damage. She is a straightforward option for turning tempo into objectives.
champions.changes: No direct changes in 26.21. This is an editorial recommendation based on her profile, not a patch buff.
weaknesses: Limited pressure before her form comes online.
Ganks depend heavily on enemy positioning.
champions.profile: Players who prefer farming, scaling and playing around objectives.

champions.name: Wukong
champions.why: He gains health regeneration but loses early armor per passive stack. His engage and teamfight impact remain valuable.
champions.changes: Health regeneration: 3.5 + 0.65/level → 5.5 + 0.65/level. Passive (Stone Skin): armor per stack 6–10 → 4.5–10 based on champion level.
strengths: Reliable engage with W and R.
weaknesses: Loses durability in the first levels.
Damage falls off without an early lead.
champions.profile: Players who want to start fights and set the pace of the map.

stats.note: ggez.gg data for all ranks. Keep watching as the sample grows.

champions.name: Nunu & Willump
champions.why: Their ultimate deals more maximum damage, but the initial patch sample does not follow: ggez.gg records a 2.6-point win-rate drop. We move them from provisional A to B until more data arrives.
champions.changes: R (Absolute Zero): maximum damage 625/925/1275 (+300% AP) → 750/1100/1450 (+300% AP).
strengths: Objective control with Q and Smite.
Can decide fights with a well-channelled R.
weaknesses: R requires channeling and can be interrupted.
The initial sample does not confirm the buff.
champions.profile: Players who prefer a straightforward jungler focused on objectives and grouped fights.

stats.note: ggez.gg data for all ranks; the initial sample is short.

champions.name: Lee Sin
champions.why: He receives a longer W cooldown and lower R damage. Even so, the early data does not sink him: he gains 0.2 points of win rate. He remains competitive in expert hands, but is no longer an automatic pick.
champions.changes: W (Safeguard): cooldown 7s → 8s. E (Tempest): no longer reveals invisible enemies who stealth after being hit. R (Dragon's Rage): damage 175/400/625 → 150/350/550 (+200% bonus AD).
strengths: Huge impact if you master his combos.
weaknesses: The nerf reduces his flexibility.
Requires a high mechanical investment.
champions.profile: Experienced players who want a tempo-driven, playmaking jungler.

stats.note: ggez.gg data for all ranks; he held up after the nerf in the initial sample.

champions.name: Nidalee
champions.why: She loses W damage and E attack speed, but the initial data actually rises 2.2 points. Her ceiling remains high in skilled hands, although the nerf hurts her clear and trading.
strengths: High damage when she lands her spear.
weaknesses: Less early attack speed.
Heavily punished when she misses her abilities.
champions.profile: Aggressive junglers with strong cougar-form control.

stats.note: ggez.gg data for all ranks; performance can vary heavily by skill.

champions.name: Rammus
champions.why: He loses defensive scaling on W and is the biggest faller in the initial sample: 3.5 points of win rate. He remains useful against heavily physical teams, but is no longer a general-purpose pick.
strengths: Simple engage with Q and crowd control.
weaknesses: The nerf lowers his durability in long fights.
Predictable and easy to counter with magic damage.
champions.profile: Players who want a straightforward tank as an answer to physical damage.

stats.note: ggez.gg data for all ranks; the largest drop among changed champions.

champions.name: Xin Zhao
champions.why: He gains better Q and E ratios and the initial data places him 3.1 points higher. We are not moving him to A because the sample is short, but he is one of the picks to watch this patch.
champions.changes: Q (Three Talon Strike): damage per strike +40% → +45% bonus AD. E (Audacious Charge): attack speed now scales with 1% per 4% permanent bonus attack speed instead of 1% per 5%.
weaknesses: Loses value without an early lead.
Can be kited in open fights.
champions.profile: Players who want a straightforward jungler with early impact.

champions.name: Orianna
champions.why: She gains AP ratios on Q and W, so her main combo hits harder later in the game. She keeps wave control, utility and a fight-deciding ultimate.
champions.changes: Q (Command: Attack): AP ratio 55% → 60%. W (Command: Dissonance): AP ratio 80% → 85%.
weaknesses: Needs good ball positioning.
Can struggle against mobile assassins.
champions.profile: Players who prefer control mages and playing around their team.

champions.name: Ryze
champions.why: He gains Q scaling, movement speed and W damage. The changes are meant to reward players who reach the later stages of the game and master his combos.
champions.changes: Q (Overload): bonus damage against Flux targets 15/40/65/90% → 10/40/70/100%. Bonus move speed 28/32/36/40/44% → 30/35/40/45/50%. W (Rune Prison): AP ratio 60% → 70%.
strengths: Very strong if he reaches late game.
weaknesses: Requires mastery of his combos.
The early game remains demanding.
champions.profile: Players willing to invest time in combos and wave management.

stats.note: ggez.gg data for all ranks; the scaling buff may take time to show.

champions.name: Fizz
champions.why: With no direct changes, he remains an effective assassin for punishing poor positioning and removing priority targets. This is an editorial recommendation.
champions.changes: No direct changes in 26.21.
strengths: Mobility with E to get in and out.
weaknesses: Relies on landing R to start.
Can run out of resources after his combo.
champions.profile: Players who enjoy assassins and creating advantages through roams.

champions.name: Gwen
champions.why: With no direct changes, she keeps a sustained-damage profile and performs well in extended fights. We include her as an editorial recommendation and her sample should be watched.
champions.changes: No direct changes in 26.21.
weaknesses: Struggles against ranged poke.
Needs time to scale.
champions.profile: Players who prefer scaling champions and extended fights.

champions.name: Azir
champions.why: He gains mana per level and the initial data rises 3.5 points. He stays on the watchlist: his difficulty and positioning requirements prevent an A placement with this sample.
champions.changes: Mana growth per level: 40 → 50.
weaknesses: Very high difficulty.
Needs to protect his soldiers and his position.
champions.profile: Experienced control-mage players willing to practise.

champions.name: Qiyana
champions.why: She loses Q damage, although the initial sample barely moves (-0.2). She remains a dangerous assassin in expert hands, but the nerf reduces her margin for error.
champions.changes: Q (Elemental Wrath / Edge of Ixtal): damage 80/110/140/170/200 (+90% bonus AD) → 70/100/130/160/190 (+90% bonus AD).
weaknesses: The nerf lowers her trading damage.
Requires precise execution.
champions.profile: Assassin players with strong mechanics and map awareness.

champions.name: Viktor
champions.why: He loses movement speed and part of his Q shield, and the initial data drops 2.4 points. He still has a strong late game, but his early game is more vulnerable.
champions.changes: Move speed: 335 → 330. Q (Siphon Power): shield 40–140 (+25% AP) → 30–130 (+20% AP).
weaknesses: More vulnerable in the early levels.
Needs time and protection.
champions.profile: Patient players who want to scale and play around their team.

champions.name: Miss Fortune
champions.why: She gains E and R damage, partly compensating for the Hubris adjustment. Her lane pressure and ultimate still punish grouped teams.
champions.changes: E (Make It Rain): damage 70/100/130/160/190 (+120% AP) → 90/120/150/180/210 (+120% AP). R (Bullet Time): critical damage 130% (+0.3% per 1% bonus crit damage) → 145% (+0.45%).
weaknesses: Needs good positioning for R.
Can struggle against dive.
champions.profile: Players who want a straightforward marksman with a clear laning plan.

stats.note: ggez.gg data for all ranks; pick rate is rising sharply.

champions.name: Kog'Maw
champions.why: With no direct changes, he keeps a sustained-damage profile and can shred durable targets when he gets time and protection.
champions.changes: No direct changes in 26.21.
weaknesses: Heavily dependent on team protection.
Low mobility.
champions.profile: Players who prefer scaling and careful positioning.

champions.name: Jinx
champions.why: She loses AD per level and base health, but keeps her scaling-carry identity and reset potential. The initial drop is 1.4 points: not a reason to discard her.
champions.changes: AD: 59 + 3.25/level → 59 + 3/level. Health: 630 + 105/level → 610 + 105/level.
weaknesses: Less room for error after the nerf.
Needs protection.
champions.profile: Players who want a patient late-game carry.

champions.name: Caitlyn
champions.why: She loses passive scaling but gains base Q damage. The change shifts power toward the laning phase, where her range still matters.
champions.changes: Passive (Headshot): 60–100% AD (+1% per 1% crit) → 60–80% AD (+0.8%). Q (Piltover Peacemaker): base damage 50/90/130/170/210 → 50/95/140/185/230.
weaknesses: Less passive damage in late game.
Depends on keeping her distance.
champions.profile: Players who want to win lane with range and pressure.

champions.name: Tristana
champions.why: She loses attack speed on the early ranks of Q and the initial data drops 2.3 points. She is still useful for tower pressure, but her early lane dominance is reduced.
weaknesses: Less early pressure after the nerf.
High risk when jumping onto targets.
champions.profile: Players who want a mobile carry with a splitpush plan.

champions.name: Varus
champions.why: The adjustments redistribute power between Q and W to limit his Top variant and allow more targeted bot tuning. In ADC he gains 2.1 points in the initial sample, but his build and skill order change.
champions.changes: Q (Piercing Arrow): damage now scales better with channel time. W (Blighted Quiver): less on-hit and per-stack damage, but better AD/AP ratios and more reward for charging Q.
weaknesses: No mobility.
Relies on landing abilities.
champions.profile: Poke players willing to adapt their build to the patch.

champions.name: Zyra
champions.why: She receives a lower W seed-ammunition cooldown. Early ggez.gg data shows a 4.3-point win-rate increase (from 50.5% to 54.8%), although this is an all-rank sample and not a guarantee of future performance.
champions.changes: W (Rampant Growth): seed ammo cooldown 18/16/14/12/10s → 16/14.5/13/11.5/10s.
strengths: Can engage with E and R.
weaknesses: Fragile if she gets caught.
Needs good seed placement.
champions.profile: Players who prefer damage supports and space control.

stats.note: ggez.gg data for all ranks; initial sample.

champions.name: Vel'Koz
champions.why: He gains passive damage and the initial data rises 2.5 points. He rewards accurate combos and can pressure from a safe distance.
champions.changes: Passive (Organic Deconstruction): 35–180 (+60% AP) → 35–205 (+65% AP).
strengths: High damage when he lands combos.
weaknesses: No mobility.
Relies on skillshots.
champions.profile: Players who prefer poke and ranged magic damage.

champions.name: Taric
champions.why: His abilities now behave more reliably when his linked ally becomes untargetable during the cast. The initial data rises 2.8 points, although his main value remains coordinated utility.
champions.changes: Q, E and R now cast correctly on untargetable allies. E (Dazzle) keeps the exception for allies who vanish from the screen. The tooltip was updated.
strengths: An R that can save entire fights.
weaknesses: Needs coordination.
Little ranged pressure.
champions.profile: Players who prefer protecting allies and playing as a team.

champions.name: Leona
champions.why: She remains a straightforward option for starting fights and chaining crowd control. Her inclusion is editorial and does not imply a direct buff in 26.21.
champions.changes: No direct changes in 26.21.
weaknesses: Low damage on her own.
Can get stuck after going in.
champions.profile: Players who want to engage and set the pace of bot lane.
